biome_based_crops.guide.title: Farmer's Field Notes
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.0.title: A living little world
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.0.body:
A greenhouse lets crops grow as though they were in another biome. It changes growing conditions, not the world outside.

1. Craft a Greenhouse Probe and a Greenhouse Core.

2. Visit the biome you want to grow. Sneak-use the probe there to take a sample. The sample stays in the probe.

3. Use the sampled probe on your core to choose that biome. You can change it later with another sample.

4. Build a sealed greenhouse, add its native blocks, and balance its temperature.

Use the probe on a crop or the core to read the last survey. The Biomes tab lists every loaded biome and its native materials.
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.1.title: Raise the glass
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.1.body:
Set the core in the floor near the centre of your growing room. Crops must be within %1$s blocks horizontally of the core.

Make a continuous floor, walls, and roof. Gaps leak the climate; close doors and trapdoors before taking a reading. Leave room for crops above the floor.

Include at least four glass blocks in the shell, with glass overhead. Glass panes also count.

Build no farther than one block beyond the growing radius. The roof must be no higher than five blocks above the core.

Place at least %2$s native specimen blocks inside the room or in its floor and walls. Any mixture of the recipe's listed materials counts. Outside decoration does not count.

Once the room is sealed, match the target climate. A valid greenhouse can satisfy exact biome and biome-tag crop rules, too.
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.2.title: Tend the temperature
biome_based_crops.guide.chapter.2.body:
The five climates run from Icy to Cold, Neutral, Warm, and Hot. Your local biome provides the starting point.

Each eight points of net heat or cold moves conditions one climate step. Opposing sources cancel. Outdoors, the change is limited to two steps. A sealed greenhouse can reach any of the five climates.

HEAT
Fire, a lit campfire, or lava: 8.
Magma block: 4.
Unlit campfires give no heat.

COOLING
Packed ice or blue ice: 8.
Ice or a snow block: 4.
A snow layer: 1.

Sources must be within the growing radius. In a greenhouse, use sources inside the room or in its shell; heat beyond the walls does not count.

Tough As Nails thermoregulators still support ordinary climate rules. They do not replace the native materials and enclosure needed for a biome greenhouse.

Take another survey after changing blocks. Conditions refresh within one second. Keep flammable plants safely away from fire.
